title: Platform CloudEvents envelope, v1
description: A narrowing profile of CloudEvents 1.0 (structured JSON mode). Every event published to the platform NATS bus MUST validate against this schema. The profile narrows CloudEvents in four places: `source` and `type` have an enforced grammar, `datacontenttype` is fixed to JSON, `dataschema` is required, and the platform extension attributes below are required on every event. `additionalProperties` is false, so a NEW OPTIONAL ATTRIBUTE IS NOT A UNILATERALLY ADDITIVE CHANGE: a producer that ships one has its events rejected by any consumer still validating against an older copy of this file. Adding an attribute is a COORDINATED ROLLOUT — every validator is updated first, producers second — and the gate pins this schema's `required` array so the ordering cannot be skipped by accident. See docs/contracts/event-contract.md.

specversion.description: CloudEvents spec version. Fixed: a second spec version would be a second contract.

id.description: Producer-assigned. Unique per (source, id). This is the de-duplication key for every at-least-once path; consumers MUST treat (source, id) as the idempotency key.

source.description: URI-reference identifying the producing component, as //<domain>/<component-path>. The domain segment is operator-supplied (the fork-ability contract: no personal domain may be hard-coded here) and the component path is stable across forks.

type.description: Reverse-DNS event type ending in an explicit major version, e.g. com.mcafeeconsulting.platform.workload.deployment.deployed.v1. The version is part of the type, never a separate attribute, so a consumer subscribing to v1 can never be handed a v2 body. The `com.mcafeeconsulting.platform.` prefix is FIXED AND A FORK DOES NOT CHANGE IT: it identifies the platform software, which a fork still runs, and is what makes an event from a forked install recognisable to the same SDK. The operator's own identity travels in `source`, which is parameterised.

subject.description: The entity the event is about, as <kind>/<namespace>/<name> for Kubernetes-scoped events. Optional per CloudEvents; required by every operator-sourced type in registry.v1.yaml.

time.description: RFC3339 with timezone, producer clock. Not usable for ordering across producers; use `sequence` within a stream.

datacontenttype.description: Fixed. A second content type is a second serialization contract and a second set of compatibility rules.

dataschema.description: Required (CloudEvents makes it optional). The JSON Schema for `data`. RESOLUTION IS DEFINED, not left to each producer: the wire value is `<contracts_base_uri>` + the registry's relative `dataschema` path, where `contracts_base_uri` is a single operator-supplied setting ending in `/` (homelab default: the raw contracts path of the operator's own fork). The registry stores the relative path and the compatibility gate compares relative paths; only the base differs between installs. A payload whose shape is not published is not a contract.

data.description: The event body. Shape is governed by `dataschema`, evolved additively within a major version: new optional fields only. Absent only for types declared `dataless: true` in the registry. The whole event — envelope plus body — must fit inside the bus message limit (subjects.v1.yaml `limits.max_event_bytes`, 1 MiB); a larger payload is referenced by URI, never embedded.

tenant.description: Platform extension. The tenancy boundary the event belongs to. Homelab publishes the reserved value `local`. This attribute is a trust boundary: a subscriber MUST NOT be delivered events whose `tenant` it is not authorized for, and authorization is enforced at the NATS account/subject level, not by consumer-side filtering.

sequence.description: Platform extension, per CloudEvents Sequence. The JetStream stream sequence, stringified, assigned on persist by the ONE stream that ingested the event (PF_EVENTS for `.ev`, PF_WORK for `.wq`); PF_AUDIT sources from PF_EVENTS and its internal sequences are never this value. Monotonic per (stream, subject) and meaningful for ordering ONLY within a single subject on a single stream — and see subjects.v1.yaml `consumers.ordering_reality` before relying on it. OPTIONAL, because only the broker can assign it: a producer does not set it, the publishing SDK fills it from the PubAck, and on the core-NATS `rq` path there is no stream and no PubAck at all. Present on every event a consumer receives from a stream; absent on a synchronous request. A required attribute that a producer must fill with a placeholder is a lie in the schema (ADR-035).

traceparent.description: W3C Trace Context. Strongly recommended and set automatically by the SDK; optional so that an event emitted outside a traced request is still valid rather than silently dropped.

tracestate.description: W3C Trace Context vendor state, carried through untouched.

correlationid.description: Platform extension. The end-to-end unit of work (e.g. a reconcile pass, a golden-path run). Distinct from traceparent, which is per-request. Required by request/reply types in the registry.

replyto.description: Platform extension. NATS inbox subject (`_INBOX.…`) for synchronous request/reply. Present ONLY on `rq` types; a consumer that sees it on a pub/sub type MUST ignore it. A `wq` durable request has no `replyto` — an inbox does not survive the wait that made the request durable — and reports its outcome through the `completion` event named in the registry.

dryrun.description: Platform extension. True when the event describes an evaluation that MUST NOT cause side effects. Consumers that cannot honour it MUST drop the event rather than act on it.
